transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-19
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Tom (Redwood Partner Ops) \u0014 Sanjay, Emily, Carlos, Leila (Aurora)

Summary:
Quick partner intro and discovery. Aurora is a cloud integrator looking to resell / co-sell Redwood inference to enterprise customers in EMEA. Primary topics: deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC), compliance (SOC2, audit logs, KMS), performance expectations (latency targets for multi-tenant SaaS), and economics / partner margins. Agreed to schedule a technical deep-dive and share security docs; Redwood to send partner one-pager + preliminary pricing.

Topics:
- Go-to-market / target customers
- Technical integration patterns (VPC peering, Private deployment)
- Benchmarks & perf expectations (latency, throughput)
- Compliance & security (SOC 2, KMS, SSO)
- Commercial model & partner margins

Transcript:
[00:00] Aisha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining \u0014 quick intros, I'm Aisha, AE at Redwood, and with me is Marcus, our SE, and Tom from partner ops.
[00:06] Sanjay: Hi, Sanjay here, Head of Cloud Partnerships at Aurora. Excited to learn about Redwood \u0014 we've had some customers ask for managed inference options.
[00:11] Marcus: Great, welcome. Quick high level from us \u0014 Redwood runs hosted APIs, dedicated reserved capacity, and private/VPC options. We try to make serving consistent across modes so you can sell the same feature set.
[00:23] Emily: Can you run through the private deployment flow? Some of our customers demand full network isolation and on-prem options.
[00:30] Marcus: Sure. For private we offer a customer-controlled control plane and can deploy into a customer VPC or on-prem. Typical pattern: we provide a bundle that your infra team or ours can deploy; we integrate with your KMS/HSM for key management, and audit logs push to your SIEM. There are a few transcribers \u0014 uh, the notes often say K V cash instead of KV cache, sorry \u0014
[00:49] Carlos: (laughs) no worries. For us, the key is whether we can meet their latency SLOs \u0014 customers want sub-200ms tail for chat-like features.
[00:58] Marcus: Totally. For chat we recommend dedicated pools with optimized kernels and KV cache warmers; that gets you lower tail latency. There's tradeoffs on cost though vs hosted.
[01:10] Sanjay: How big are we talking for dedicated? If a customer needs say 20 steady concurrent sessions at 4k tokens are we in multi-GPU territory?
[01:18] Marcus: It depends on model and quantization; rough back-of-envelope a few A100 or equivalent for high throughput \u0014 we can map out a sizing chart. We'll also recommend batching and prefix caching to reduce per-token cost.
[01:30] Leila: From a partner motion, we're more interested in how easy it is to onboard customers and to replicate setups. Do you have templates / IaC?
[01:37] Tom: Yes \u0014 we provide Terraform modules and deployment runbooks for private and dedicated setups; plus a partner portal with reference architectures. We'll share the repo link after the call.
[01:47] Emily: Compliance \u0014 SOC2 is table stakes for our enterprise customers, plus they ask for SSO (SAML/Okta) and RBAC. How mature are your controls?
[01:56] Aisha: We're SOC2 Type II; we support SAML/Okta SSO and fine-grained RBAC. Audit logs can be exported and we have retention controls. We'll share the security pack.
[02:06] Carlos: Data residency \u0014 some customers need EU-only processing. Can Redwood pin regions?
[02:11] Marcus: Yes you can pin regions and we can deploy private in-region stacks. For hosted we also support region controls and data residency options for enterprise plans.
[02:21] Sanjay: Commercial question \u0014 what's the partner margin model? Resell vs referral?
[02:26] Aisha: We have a partner program with both referral and reseller options. Typical reseller margin bands depend on committed volume. We'll share draft partner economics; Tom will kick off the legal paperwork for reseller agreements if you want.
[02:37] Leila: Awesome. A bit more technical \u0014 what's your model catalog? Do you bring open models only or provide proprietary models?
[02:44] Marcus: We curate open models and Redwood-verified performance profiles; we also host some optimized variants. For high-accuracy customers we recommend the larger variants, but we also provide quantized versions for cost.
[02:55] Sanjay: Any partners doing managed benchmarks? Customers like to see A vs B comparisons.
[03:01] Marcus: We can run benchmark jobs for a POC \u0014 we usually ask partners to provide a representative prompt set and target SLOs. We'll run on both hosted and dedicated and share token-level cost and latency breakdowns.
[03:13] Emily: On networking, do you do VPC peering or private link?
[03:17] Marcus: We support VPC peering, PrivateLink-equivalent setups, and can stitch in with transit gateways. For on-prem we use a VPN or direct connect.
[03:26] Carlos: How do you handle fallbacks if a dedicated pool is saturated? Some customers can't afford errors.
[03:31] Marcus: Smart routing. We have policy-based routing that can fail over to a compatible model or a hosted tier; fallback granularity is per-route. You can configure canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallback policies.
[03:45] Sanjay: Security follow-up: do you support customer-managed keys and HSM integration?
[03:49] Aisha: Yes, KMS/HSM integrations are supported for private and enterprise offerings.
[03:54] Leila: A couple of real asks from our pipeline: 1) A finance SaaS customer in UK needs EU-only processing and SOC2 plus monthly audit logs. 2) A health-tech startup needs private on-prem for PHI. They'd like an estimate and timeline.
[04:07] Aisha: For the finance customer EU-only hosted/dedicated is doable; for health-tech on-prem tends to be a few weeks to stand up depending on access. We'll send a sizing + timelines.
[04:17] Marcus: For on-prem PHI we usually recommend an initial pilot with limited traffic to validate and then scale. Also, quantization profiles can reduce hardware needs.
[04:27] Sanjay: Any red flags on the regulatory side? HIPAA / PHI support?
[04:31] Aisha: We have guidance for HIPAA customers \u0014 private deployment and BAA conversations are standard. We'll route legal to work with yours.
[04:39] Emily: Integrations \u0014 do you have SDKs and prebuilt connectors for things like Kafka, SQS, or batch inference?
[04:46] Marcus: Yes, SDKs in Python/Node and connectors for common queues; we also have a batch inference runner.
[04:52] Leila: For co-sell, timeline matters. We have a few deals that might close in Q2; what's your typical timeline to onboard a partner and get first POC done?
[04:59] Tom: Partner onboarding and NDA is usually 1 week; first POC can be 2-6 weeks depending on complexity. For dedicated capacity procurement we sometimes need more lead time.
[05:11] Sanjay: On hosting, can you offer committed reserved capacity that we can reassign to customers?
[05:16] Aisha: We have Dedicated reserved pools \u0014 usually committed by the customer but there are partner programs where we can carve partner-managed pools. We'll detail the commercial options.
[05:25] Marcus: Small note \u0014 sometimes the transcript auto-generates weird names for our product features; you'll see Redwood Optimize or Redwood Dedicated in docs, but in speech it can get butchered.
[05:34] Carlos: (laughs) understood.
[05:36] Emily: A question from my engineering view \u0014 if a customer wants model pinning and strict versioning for rollouts, is that a first-class feature?
[05:44] Marcus: Yes we support model version pinning, canary rollouts, and automatic rollback. We tie quality monitoring to prompt sets so you can detect regressions.
[05:52] Sanjay: For benchmarks, what metrics do you return? We want per-token cost and 95/99 latencies.
[05:59] Marcus: We provide token-level cost, p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput, error rates, and memory/kv cache metrics. We'll include the benchmark spreadsheet.
[06:12] Leila: Regarding partner enablement, do you provide co-marketing assets and joint case studies?
[06:17] Aisha: Yes \u0014 co-marketing, joint decks, and one-pagers. We'll also help with demo environments for joint sales calls.
[06:25] Sanjay: Any specific customers you recommend we reference?
[06:29] Aisha: We can share anonymized case studies and references \u0014 privacy rules apply but we'll coordinate through Tom.
[06:36] Emily: Network question again \u0014 is there an outbound IP allowlist for hosted API? Our customers sometimes require static egress IPs.
[06:43] Marcus: We can provide ranges for enterprise tenants; for stricter cases we recommend private deployment.
[06:50] Carlos: On observability, do you expose per-route traces and token-level cost to customers?
[06:56] Marcus: Yes, Redwood Console shows per-route/model dashboards, tracing hooks, error analysis, and token-level cost. You can integrate traces into your APM.
[07:06] Sanjay: OK \u0014 time for a quick recap of next steps?
[07:10] Aisha: Sure. We'll send partner one-pager, security pack, and pricing. Marcus will schedule the technical deep-dive to run benchmarks. Tom will start onboarding/NDA. Aurora to share target customers and compliance requirements.
[07:22] Leila: Perfect. Is there any reason we shouldn't start a reseller conversation?
[07:27] Aisha: No \u0014 happy to. We'll kick off reseller docs.
[07:31] Carlos: Curious \u0014 who do we contact on partner support during POC?
[07:35] Tom: That will be me and a named SE \u0014 Marcus will be your SE for the first POC.
[07:40] Sanjay: Great. We'll look for the docs. Thanks everyone.
[07:44] Aisha: Thanks, talk soon.

(Transcript continues with brief Q&A and clarifications, some cross-talk and filler; timestamps above are approximate \u0014 meeting ran to ~46 minutes, several sections condensed here.)

Final recap (from notes):
- Redwood to share: partner one-pager + pricing ranges, security pack (SOC2, KMS, BAA guidance), benchmark template, Terraform modules link.
- Aurora to share: list of target customers, regional/compliance requirements, initial PII/PHI use cases for scoping.
- Schedule: tech deep-dive / benchmark slot (Marcus to propose 2 slots next week).
- Paperwork: Tom to send NDA + partner onboarding docs.

References mentioned:

End of transcript.
